title: Crystal Palace’s Cheick Doucoure plays first match after 14-month layoff with knee injury
content:
Cheick Doucoure played for Crystal Palace’s under-21 side on Friday — his first appearance in more than a year after suffering a knee injury.

Doucoure started the game and completed the first half before being substituted at half-time in a planned move as the midfielder appeared to come through unscathed.

The 26-year-old tore his meniscus in January 2025, having played just 13 times since recovering from a ruptured achilles suffered in a 2-1 defeat by Luton Town in November 2023.

It has been a long road back to recovery for Doucoure who was Palace’s player of the year in the 2022-23 season — his debut campaign having joined from Lens that summer in a deal worth up to £26million including add-ons.

Doucoure’s meniscus injury came after two successive starts following a sustained period on the sidelines.

The midfielder, who played in Friday’s under-21 game against Blackburn Rovers,  is not registered for Palace’s Conference League squad but could return this season for the Premier League run-in.

Before Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle United in January, Glasner said in his press conference that they had hoped Doucoure would have been available before Christmas only for that to have fallen behind schedule, while he spoke positively about the Mali international before the 3-1 Carabao Cup victory over Liverpool in October.

“Cheick is tough,” Glasner said. “It’s tough for him. In the gym. I’m really suffering when I have to talk about it, because he’s such a lovely man, always positive, always smiling but can’t leave the gym now for a month. It looks better than a few weeks ago but he’s had a few setbacks. I can’t tell you any timeline but I think he won’t play in 2025.”

Palace face a three-week break at the end of March without a game due to an international break and not being involved in the FA Cup, meaning Doucoure might return for the home game with Newcastle United on April 11.

Doucoure signed a new contract in February last year to extend his deal with Palace until 2029.
